portrait.sp106r787: Writer unknown (signs with numbers; Lasry suggests Dr Stephen Goffe in Holland, untested) and the receiver is uncertain (the Queen or the King); no person can be named for either side.
portrait.sp106r929: Writer unknown (signs 316 440) and the receiver is an unnamed 'Sir' at the King's side; no person can be named for either side.

portrait.jantini1517: Sender Benedetto Fantini, a Ferrarese agent in Hungary, has no known portrait; the recipient ('V. S. Ill.ma') is unidentified.
portrait.marburg1635: Writer and recipient are both unknown (an anonymous officer or agent reporting to Kassel).
portrait.harley286: Private cipher record, no recipient; Sir Simonds D'Ewes has no identified portrait on Wikimedia Commons (no Wikidata P18; Commons has his monument and ledger slab). portrait.harley7001: Writer Robert Reade (Windebank's nephew and secretary) and his cousin, probably Thomas Windebank, have no portraits on Wikimedia Commons (no Wikidata image for either).
portrait.r688: Stojan and the writer Mla[den?] Baki[ć?] are unidentified private people; no portraits exist.
portrait.r4349: Not a letter between people: an anonymous Dominican scribe's colophon for a convent (Strängnäs for Västerås).
portrait.andreae1616: A printed novel, not a letter between people; no sender or recipient.
portrait.mellon29: Not a letter between people: an alchemical book pseudonymously ascribed to Elias of Cortona (d. 1253), copied c. 1525 by an unknown scribe; no sender or recipient.

portrait.r1862: The sender is an unidentified Venetian ambassador at Rome (the letter does not name him); the recipient is an office, the Doge and Senate.
portrait.r4817: Anonymous alchemical annotation, no identifiable sender or recipient; Mögling wrote the work but is not established as the annotator.
portrait.segura1596: No verified portrait of Matheo de Segura located; recipient search found a group portrait without a verified individual crop.
portrait.potocka1714: Commons searches found namesakes, not a verified public-domain portrait of Barbara Dunin Potocka or Jakub Antoni Dunin.
portrait.mniszech1714: Recipient side only: Commons searches found namesakes, not a verified public-domain portrait of Jakub Antoni Dunin (as for potocka1714); the sender, Józef Wandalin Mniszech, has his portrait.
portrait.riksarkivet4284: Sender unnamed and recipient only conjectured (a later archival note files it with the letters to Ludwig Camerarius), so no portrait pair can be verified.
portrait.riksarkivet4306: Sender unknown and the addressee, a 'Mr ...ilick' at Amsterdam, unidentified.
portrait.r2276: The letter is unsigned (the writer is probably Jean de Piles, abbé d'Orbais, who has no known portrait) and the addressee is not named.
portrait.benedict1399: Recipient side only: Francesc Climent Sapera (Çapera) has no trustworthy portrait on Wikimedia Commons (Wikidata Q68866337 has no image); sender Benedict XIII has one.
portrait.indus: Not a letter between people: undeciphered Bronze Age seals and tablets, no named sender or recipient.
portrait.lineara: Not correspondence: anonymous Minoan scribes and administrators; no named sender or recipient.
portrait.ilten1743: Recipient Johann Georg von Ilten (1688-1749) and sender Ernst von Steinberg (Hanoverian minister in London) have no portrait on Wikimedia Commons (Wikidata Q28374583 and Q5395212 carry no image; Commons search found none); the other letter is unsigned.
portrait.siena1421: The unread pieces of a bundle addressed to the Sienese government (the Concistoro, the Balia, the Priori: offices), mostly from unnamed envoys; Donato Acciaiuoli (no. 11) has only a photograph of a herm on Commons, excluded.
portrait.siena25: Unsigned slip from unnamed Sienese envoys to the Signoria (an office).
portrait.siena18: Articles between the Sienese orators (unnamed) and the imperial side; the subscriber Niccolo Ziegler, a secretary, has no portrait on Wikimedia Commons or Wikidata, and the other parties are offices.
portrait.siena14: From envoys signing only '...Marco' to the Priori and Capitano del Popolo (offices).
portrait.borghesi1456: Galgano Borghesi and Leonardo Benvoglienti have no portrait on Wikimedia Commons or Wikidata (searched 25 Sept 2026).
portrait.hesse1824: Sender given only as 'Snell' (Wilhelm or Ludwig Snell, not settled from the leaf); the addressee's name in the heading is not made out, so no portrait can be tied to either side.
portrait.szembek1689: The writer and the recipient ('Reverendissime Pater') are not named in the postscript; Şerban Cantacuzino and Dunod are its subjects, not its correspondents.
portrait.vizani1637: Sender Fra Guglielmo Vizani, a Roman agent at Constantinople, has no known portrait; none of Philippe de Harlay, comte de Césy, was found on Wikimedia Commons.
portrait.sp106r927: Sender anonymous: the letter is signed with a name read 'Nicle'(?) at Nancy, not identified; the recipient is addressed only as 'Monsieur'. No person to portray.
portrait.orbais: sender is an unnamed secretary of Cardinal Pellevé; no portrait of the recipient Jean de Piles, abbé d'Orbais, on Wikimedia Commons (searched 5 Oct 2026)
portrait.battier1686: No verified portrait of Pieter Battier or Gaspar Fagel was found among the site's portraits; no namesake image was used.
portrait.aerssen1601: No verified portrait of François van Aerssen or Johan van Oldenbarnevelt was added with this contribution; to check on Wikimedia Commons.
portrait.beuningen1676: No verified portrait of either correspondent was added with this contribution.
portrait.esterhazy1744: The one document online names neither its writer nor its sovereign ('Votre Majesté'); the Maria Theresa letter of box 636 is not online, so no correspondent of a visible document is identified.
portrait.hesse1672: The writer's signature is not made out and HCPortal names neither side; the recipient is addressed only as 'Herr Canzler' (the Hessian chancellor), an office, so no portrait can be tied to either side.
portrait.sieniawski1708: Several correspondences on one page; the principal one (the Vienna letters) is from an unidentified agent signing with a cover name ('Sidon') to a Baron Schenck, chamberlain of Augustus II, who has no identified portrait (no Wikidata item or Commons image found).
portrait.ottobon: No trustworthy public-domain portrait on Commons or Wikidata (searched 9 Oct 2026) of the subscribing secretary Marco Ottobon (1554-1649) or of the ambassador Giovanni Mocenigo (not the doge of that name); the sender proper is the Doge and Senate as a body.
portrait.voynich: Not a letter between people: an anonymous early-15th-century codex with no named author or recipient.
portrait.siena1431: Sender Cristofano (surname damaged, perhaps Montucci) is not identified and has no known portrait; the recipients are the Signori of Siena as a body.
portrait.decode4282: Sender and recipient are unidentified; no verified person can be portrayed.
portrait.ranzo1528: Writer Hieronimo Ranzo, a Vercelli nobleman at Charles V's court, has no known portrait; 'Garbino' is a cover name and Ranzo's other correspondents are unidentified.

reveal.matignon1586c3: The readings (read_final.txt) record one letter per sign, not the sign forms, and no sign-level transcription keyed to Tomokiyo's table is committed, so a replay would invent the signs.
reveal.dubellay1528: Read from Bourrilly and de Vaissière's printed clear text (1905); their key is not printed, Lasry's exists only as an image, and no transcription of the cipher was made here, so no passage can be replayed sign by sign.
reveal.federico1497: Read from Ivan Parisi's printed decipherment; no sign-level transcription of no. 5 was made here, so a replay would invent the alignment.
reveal.esp318no95: The sign-level reading lives only as git-ignored glyph clusters (targets/esp318/f122r_glyphs.pkl); the committed reading is by verified stretches, not sign by sign, so a replay would invent the alignment.
reveal.esp318no93: Not deciphered: no key, so no passage can be decoded sign by sign.
reveal.segur1583: Not solved: nothing in f. 143 is deciphered, so there is no passage to replay.
reveal.langeac1529: The eleven cipher lines were deciphered by eye from line strips against Lasry's table and no sign-by-sign alias transcription was kept (18 Sept 2026), so a replay would invent the sign alignment; a glyph transcription of Gallica view 36 would allow one.
reveal.gramont1530: The fourteen cipher lines were deciphered by eye from line strips against Lasry's table and no sign-by-sign alias transcription was kept (18 Sept 2026), so a replay would invent the sign alignment; a glyph transcription of Gallica view 30 is the next step.
reveal.r4248: Read from the contemporary clear decipherment on f. 86; the f. 85 cipher was not transcribed sign by sign and its key not tabulated, so no passage can be replayed without inventing the alignment.
reveal.sabran1631: Read from George Lasry's published decipherment, which exists only as capitals overlaid on the image (GL.htm); no transcription of f. 79r was made here and his key was not applied, so a sign-by-sign replay would invent the alignment.
reveal.brulart1615: Read from Satoshi Tomokiyo's reading with his key; no transcription of R2785 or R2786 was made here and the key was not applied, so no passage can be replayed sign by sign without inventing the alignment.
reveal.r1873: Read from Bonavoglia's published decipherment: his transcription and his plaintext are not aligned sign by sign and no key was rebuilt here, so a token-by-token replay would invent the alignment.
reveal.r1871: Not solved: no value is known for any of the 211 three-digit groups, so no passage can be replayed sign by sign.
reveal.mniszech1714: Not solved: no value is known for any of the 232 figures, so no passage can be replayed sign by sign.
reveal.riksarkivet4284: Not solved: no value is known for any of the number groups, so no passage can be replayed sign by sign.

reveal.riksarkivet4306: Not solved: no value is known for any of the number groups, so no passage can be replayed sign by sign.

atlas.matignon1586c3: Unsigned and unaddressed: no place of writing or receipt is given.
atlas.dubellay1528: From London, 28 Oct 1528, to Montmorency with the court; where the court was on arrival is not established in the folder (the preceding letter in Bourrilly is from Fontainebleau, 26 Oct).
atlas.federico1497: Sent from San Germano to the Catholic Monarchs; where the court was on receipt in January 1497 is not established from the letter.
atlas.esp318: The Great Captain's place of writing on 17 Aug 1500 is not given on the leaf (the copy went to Almazán); left off the map.
atlas.esp318no93: Venice and Messina are known, but where the Catholic Monarchs and Ferdinand were on receipt (1503, 1504) is not established from the letters.
atlas.laigue1649: From Paris, 5 March 1649, to Laigue with Archduke Leopold Wilhelm's army; where the Archduke's camp was that week is not established in the folder.
atlas.hm1645: St Germain to Charles I in September 1645, when the King was on the move after Naseby (Hereford, Raglan, Chester, Newark); the receiving place of each letter is not established, so they are left off the map.
atlas.sp106r787: Writer and place of writing unknown (Lasry: perhaps Goffe in Holland); receiver uncertain.
atlas.sp106r929: Written at Paris to an unnamed 'Sir' with the King; the receiver's place is not established.
atlas.rohan1636: Sent from the army in Piedmont (the camp is not fixed by the print) to Rohan in the Valtellina; no city established for either end.
atlas.emery1636: D'Émery's place of writing and Rohan's position in January 1636 are not established from the letters, which have not been seen.
atlas.riksarkivet4284: Sender and place of writing unknown; only a later archival note links it to Camerarius's file for 1628.
atlas.riksarkivet4306: Sender and place of writing unknown; only the addressee's town, Amsterdam, is known.
atlas.rusdorff1628: From The Hague, 1628; where Oxenstierna (then mostly in Prussia) received each letter is not established.
atlas.oxenstierna1633: The writer and his place of writing are not identified; Oxenstierna's whereabouts in June 1633 not checked letter by letter.
atlas.mniszech1714: From Dukla, 18 March 1714; where Jakub Dunin, the Crown regent, received it is not established.
atlas.labbe1582: Origins known, destination only France; no city established for Nevers at either date.
atlas.indus: Not letters: seals and tablets from some fifty sites, no sender or destination.
atlas.ilten1743: Both letters are from London; Ilten was with the Hanoverian troops in the Low Countries and no city is established for him in Feb-Apr 1743.
atlas.siena1421: The unread pieces are mostly undated and unplaced; no. 11 (Rome to Florence, 1478) is a Florentine intercept whose route is not this bundle's; left out rather than guessed.
atlas.siena25: The slip names neither its place of writing nor its date; left out rather than guessed.
atlas.siena18: Articles negotiated at an unnamed imperial court, undated; left out rather than guessed.
atlas.siena14: The place of writing (Rome?) is doubtful and the date unknown; left out rather than guessed.
atlas.borghesi1456: From Naples, but where the recipient Benvoglienti was on 12 May 1456 is not certain; left out rather than guessed.
atlas.burgo1527: The minute gives no place or year; the Emperor's whereabouts cannot be fixed without guessing.
atlas.hesse1824: Neither the sender's place (Basel or Wetzlar) nor the addressee's is established from the leaf.
atlas.waldeck1744: Destination known (the Prince of Waldeck, who served with the Austrian army in 1744), but the writer's place is not named; left out rather than guessed.
atlas.aerssen1601: Paris origin established; Oldenbarnevelt recipient location not established in supplied evidence. No guessed route.
atlas.esterhazy1744: Origin Moscow, but the recipient and destination of the visible letter are not established.
atlas.siena1431: Neither letter names its place of writing; the writer reports from the Milanese side of the war over Lucca but his location is not established.
atlas.decode4282: Origin and destination are unknown; the catalogue range 1600–1699 does not establish a route or document date.
